audit_findings.title: The trend anchor appears contaminated by a large noncash pension-settlement charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $70.5 million filed 2023 charge; mechanically adding it to 2023 OE raises the log-trend anchor about $6.5 million and bull value about $1.38 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining an exceptional noncash charge depresses the 2023 OE observation and therefore the fitted log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The amounts for the year ended December 31, 2023 do not include a non-cash charge of $ 70.5 million related to the completion of the buy-out of the UK pension plan and a gain of $ 1.9 million related to excess assets from the UK pension plan that reverted back to the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge is demonstrated, but its treatment in OE remains unreconciled. Even assuming it was wholly and incorrectly retained, the computed bull value rises only from $16.75 to about $18.13 per share, still far below the $91.98 market price. Even mechanically adding the full filed 2023 pension charge plus the $50.0 million 2024 and $37.8 million 2025 other-operating charges would raise bull value only to about $21.23 per share. It cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each annual OE observation to GAAP income and cash flow, identify the tax and cash character of the 2023 pension settlement and 2024-2025 charges, and retain the corrected trend rerun as an audit trail.

audit_findings.title: A null perimeter conflicts with businesses exited during 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical OE and maintenance capital may include operations absent from the forecast perimeter, while disposal proceeds and exit costs may be treated inconsistently.
audit_findings.evidence: In early 2025, the Company divested its Hartford, Connecticut additive printing business and in June 2025, the Company closed its Welkenraedt, Belgium engineered products facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: Austria, Hartford and Welkenraedt were exited, while the valuation records no perimeter adjustment. Austria's filed sales declined from $56.1 million in 2023 to $38.1 million in 2024 and $27.0 million in 2025, but sales do not establish OE, maintenance capital or stranded-cost effects. Hartford and Belgium contributions are also not separately quantified. The record therefore cannot establish either direction or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Prepare continuing-operations OE schedules for Austria, Hartford, Welkenraedt and the former Malaysia joint venture, including allocated overhead, maintenance capital, exit costs and disposal proceeds, then rerun the full OE series and anchor.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized borrowing costs may escape both OE and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.2 million in 2025 and $32.6 million cumulatively for 2023-2025; treating $15.2 million as a wholly omitted recurring cost would reduce bull value by about $3.23 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If capitalized interest is absent from earnings and excluded from the maintenance-capex deduction, OE is overstated; the equity-level bridge does not otherwise capture it.
audit_findings.evidence: Capitalized interes t of $ 15.2 millio n, $ 10.7 million, and $ 6.7 million for 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, was included in construction in progress.
audit_findings.explanation: The capitalized amounts are demonstrated, but double omission is only a possibility until the OE workpapers are traced. Even under the adverse assumption that the entire 2025 amount was omitted and recurs indefinitely, bull value falls from $16.75 to about $13.52 per share, which does not change the conclusion relative to the $91.98 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized interest through operating cash flow, construction-in-progress additions and the maintenance-capex calculation; if absent, deduct it exactly once and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded pension balance is a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.0 million filed 2025 deficit, equal to about $0.22 per share and 1.5% of base equity value; June 2026 aggregate retirement obligations were $28.8 million
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded obligation attributable to prior service is a senior claim that may require a bridge deduction beyond normalized pension expense.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the total benefit obligation was $ 21.0 million, and the fair value of plan assets was $ 4.0 million, resulting in a net projected benefit obligation ("PBO") of $ 17.0 million ($ 2.4 million recorded in current liabilities and $ 14.6 million in other non-current liabilities).
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 deficit and absence of a pension bridge adjustment are demonstrated. Deducting the full $17.0 million would lower base value from $14.32 to about $14.10 per share. Even deducting all $28.8 million of June 2026 retirement obligations would reduce value by only about $0.37 per share, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 plan-level funded status, separate ordinary accrued benefits from any true incremental deficit, quantify multi-employer withdrawal exposure, and record any non-duplicative bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: Environmental exposure could materially exceed the recorded reserve
audit_findings.mechanism: Any liability above the recorded reserve would be a senior cash claim requiring a bridge deduction or, if recurring, a reduction to OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Because the Federal Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (“CERCLA” or “Superfund”) allows for joint and several liability in certain circumstances, we could be responsible for all remediation costs at such sites, even if we are one of many PRPs.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending Lower Passaic proceedings, joint-and-several-liability mechanism and $0.1 million reserve are demonstrated. The filed gross remediation ranges and $150 million collective escrow do not identify Hexcel's allocated share, recoveries or probability of loss. Consequently, the record cannot determine whether exposure above the reserve is immaterial or large enough to affect the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the allocator recommendation, Hexcel's escrow contribution, appeal status through September 5, 2026, contribution claims, insurance and indemnification recoveries, and counsel's probability range; rerun the bridge using probability-weighted and adverse-case deductions.

audit_findings.title: Cash may not be fully distributable at face value
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge exposure of $62.2 million, equal to about $0.80 per share and 5.6% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Trapped cash, repatriation costs or required operating cash would reduce the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we have approximately $ 204.0 million of unremitted foreign earnings that we intend to keep indefinitely reinvested.
audit_findings.explanation: The $204.0 million of indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings is demonstrated, but it does not establish that the June 2026 cash is trapped. Accessibility remains unresolved. Nevertheless, even removing the entire $62.2 million cash bridge—an upper bound exceeding any tax-only adjustment—would lower bull value from $16.75 to about $15.95 per share and cannot change the conclusion relative to $91.98.
audit_findings.action: Map the $62.2 million by jurisdiction and legal entity, quantify withholding and repatriation taxes, restrictions and minimum operating cash, then rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.
